author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if just doing some good isn’t actually good enough? Jon Bogard challenges us to confront the uncomfortable truth: Our instincts about helping others are often flawed. Cognitive “bugs” like opportunity cost neglect, the “warm glow” feeling of giving, and scope insensitivity lead us to make choices that selfishly feel meaningful but fall short of real impact.

Given that the world’s problems are bigger than the number of people rushing in to help, how can we use our lives to do the most good possible? What if just doing some good isn’t actually good enough? 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Do your acts of kindness make a real impact? | Jon Bogard | TEDxWUSTL

author: TEDx Talks
description: Climate disasters don’t respect borders or visas - when they strike, the only question is how fast we can help one another. With COP31 approaching, Ambassador of Türkiye to Bulgaria Mehmet Sait Uyanık reveals how navigating geopolitics and climate justice at the crossroads of three continents proves that global solidarity is our only path forward. With a strong focus on COP31, Ambassador Mehmet Sait Uyanık brings Türkiye’s climate policies to the forefront. He shares the experience of a  nation situated between Europe, Asia, and the Middle East to tackle geopolitics, energy, and climate justice, and to accelerate global electrification and Net Zero emissions. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Neighbours need each other for a handful of ash | Mehmet Sait Uyanık | TEDxVitosha

Rivers do not stop at borders, so who decides how their water is shared? 
Mahnaz Lashkri turns to transnational water governance, one of the world’s most contested resources, and shows how the way we talk shapes what we share. A resource that crosses borders needs conversations that cross them too.

This talk was part of the first edition of TEDxEuropean University Institute Florence, held at Palazzo Buontalenti, home to the Florence School of Transnational Governance of the European University Institute (EUI), in the former courtroom of the Court of Appeal of Florence (Italy).

Theme: “Agents of Change”. Mahnaz Lashkri is Strategic Projects and Partnerships Manager at the University of Kurdistan Hewlêr (UKH). She is a co-founding member of UKH’s Center for Peacebuilding and Dialogue. She holds a BA with honours in Politics and International Relations and an MA in International Studies, both from UKH. 
She has worked in government and the humanitarian sector on policy, community-led a
title: How We Talk Shapes What We Share | Mahnaz Lashkri | TEDxEuropean University Institute Florence

description:
A reaction on social media takes a second. Margarita Iliopoulou asks whether it matters far more than you think, linking it to digital bank runs and misinformation. In a financial system that runs on trust, what spreads online can have real consequences.

This talk was part of the first edition of TEDxEuropean University Institute Florence, held at Palazzo Buontalenti, home to the Florence School of Transnational Governance of the European University Institute (EUI), in the former courtroom of the Court of Appeal of Florence (Italy).

Theme: “Agents of Change”. Margarita Iliopoulou is Senior Legal Expert at the EU Single Resolution Board. She is a legal counsel and economist specialising in banking regulation and digital transformation. She has advised on banking supervision and resolution across six jurisdictions, from Berlin to Washington. title: How Online Actions Become Crises | Margarita Iliopoulou | TEDxEuropean University Institute Florence

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The joy of music with Pavan Bhat at TEDxGCEM.

Through a captivating musical session, Pavan Bhat brought rhythm, melody, and energy to the TEDxGCEM stage, creating a memorable experience for the audience. 

This musical session celebrates the power of music to transcend words, evoke emotions, and bring people together.

Because sometimes, a melody is all it takes to create a connection.

 

 Pavan Bhat is a Kannada singer, performer, and storyteller who is on a mission to bring people together through music. Known for his Kannada Retro-Jamming experiences, Pavan has created a unique space where audiences don’t just listen to music; they sing along, participate, and become part of the performance. From children and young adults to parents and senior citizens, his shows bring generations together through the nostalgia and emotion of Kannada music. What began as a passion for music has grown into a community-driven movement, with Pavan performing across Karnataka and creating experiences
title: A Musical Experience with Pavan Bhat | Pavan Bhat | TEDxGCEM

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if... the person you were meant to become isn't the person everyone expects you to be? Who shaped us into the people we want to be? Now I want you guys to think about it for a moment. Then, picture this. An elite boarding school. Generations of students prepared to become doctors, lawyers, even engineers — people who will eventually become somebody.
 A student at Cahaya Rancamaya with a passion for movies, books, and storytelling. She is
curious about individuality, success, and the expectations society places on young people. After
an unsuccessful attempt to join TEDx in Grade 10, she tried again the following year and earned
a place in the program. Through her TEDx talk, she hopes to challenge conventional definitions
of success and encourage others to discover their own paths to fulfillment. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: WHO TAUGHT YOU WHAT TO BECOME? | Kinanti Sakalaguna Prasetyo | TEDxCRIBS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if you're not afraid of failing, but afraid of being seen succeeding? Taylor M. LaSane explores how success can threaten our sense of belonging, causing us to hide from our own potential. She challenges us to rethink what holds us back and find the courage to be visible before we feel ready. "Taylor M. LaSane is a consultant, facilitator, and founder of SHYNE, a career studio helping leaders navigate change. A certified leadership coach trained through Brown University and Harvard Business School Online, Taylor combines executive strategy, neuroscience, and Scripture to help people move from uncertainty to intentional action.

Taylor spent nearly a decade at Google leading executive communications and organizational change initiatives impacting more than 150,000 employees globally. Today, she brings that same strategic lens to individuals, teams, and organizations navigating growth, transformation, and visibility.  A Detroit native, wife, twin mom, and Howard University alumna, T
title: Why Visibility Feels Scarier Than Failure | Taylor M. LaSane | TEDxBuckheadAve

description:

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this TED Talk, Taihong Pan shares how a small, scratched 300-yuan telescope on a sixth-floor balcony changed the way he sees the sky—and himself. The first time he looked at the moon, he screamed: it wasn't the smooth, shiny coin he'd imagined, but a rocky, pitted world. That shock sparked a habit of questioning what he thought he knew. Through his father, he learned Venus is a planet, not a star; through The Space Encyclopedia, he discovered that Chang'e is not just a fairy tale but a real lunar probe that brought 1,731 grams of moon soil home. He also speaks honestly about nearly giving up on a math problem, watching rockets explode and be rebuilt, and realizing that space exploration depends on thousands of unnamed workers, not just famous astronauts. His message: being wrong is not failure—every corrected mistake brings us closer to the real sky. Chasing stars isn't about catching one; it's about keeping your head up, keep asking questions, and keep being surprised. As a studen
title: The moon is not round | Taihong Pan | TEDxGrand School Qingdao Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this deeply personal and reflective talk, Mark Hsueh explores the hopes, values, and life lessons he wishes to pass on to the next generation. Through the imagined form of a letter to his future daughter, he reflects on love, family, identity, and the kind of world he hopes she will grow up in. Beyond the expectations of parenthood, Mark invites us to consider what truly matters when shaping another person's future: the values we model, the wisdom we share, and the freedom we give others to discover their own paths. His talk offers a thoughtful reflection on legacy, responsibility, and the enduring power of love. Teacher of English at Guangzhou Ulink International School-NCPA Division This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: A Letter to My Future Daughter | Mark Hsueh | TEDxGUIS Guangzhou Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if your career wasn't meant to follow a straight line? Meryem challenges the traditional idea of climbing the career ladder, encouraging us to see our professional journeys as maps filled with different paths, unexpected turns, and endless opportunities. Meryem Ben Elajla, photonics expert, deep-tech professional, and someone whose career has taken her across research, technology, business and everything in between.

Having explored so many different paths, Meryem knows firsthand that a career rarely moves in one straight direction. In her talk, she challenges the traditional career ladder and asks: what if we stopped climbing and started mapping instead? This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why your career needs a map, not a ladder | Meryem Ben Elajla | TEDxVUB

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Dans quel État vivez-vous ? La France, l’Estonie, le Portugal… Personne ne répond « l’Union européenne ». Depuis le fameux « objet politique non identifié » de Jacques Delors, on a pris l’habitude de ne pas trop se demander ce qu’elle est vraiment.

L’historien Sylvain Kahn propose de briser ce tabou. Selon lui, l’UE est un État, à sa manière. Les Européens ont inventé des cités-États, des monarchies, des empires, et même un Saint-Empire qui a duré mille ans ; l’Union serait simplement la dernière de ces formes. Il montre le moment où, selon lui, elle a basculé : la nuit du 20 au 21 juillet 2020, quand les Vingt-Sept ont décidé d’emprunter ensemble 750 milliards d’euros sur les marchés pour faire face au Covid. Une monnaie, une cour de justice, des lois votées par des élus : c’est un « État d’États », qui met en réseau la souveraineté de ses membres au lieu de la leur prendre.

Et si l’on reconnaissait que nous avons deux États, la question ne serait plus « faut-il en sortir ? » mais
title: L'Union Européenne, dans tous ses états ! | Sylvain Kahn | TEDxVersailles Grand Parc

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Que restera-t-il de nos métiers quand l’intelligence artificielle saura tout concevoir et tout calculer ? Jim de Missolz est serrurier. Pas celui qui ouvre les portes : celui qui forge des grilles, des escaliers et du mobilier, et qui restaure le patrimoine. Formé dix ans sur les routes du Compagnonnage, il a repris un atelier parisien où l’enclume résonne depuis 1893. Il en est aujourd’hui la cinquième génération.

Il ne refuse pas le progrès : l’IA lui fait gagner un temps précieux dans ses études. Mais une machine sait-elle pourquoi on fabrique un objet ? Reconnaît-elle la beauté d’une imperfection, la valeur d’un geste transmis de main en main ? Selon lui, le danger n’est pas que la machine fasse à notre place. C’est que nous oubliions comment faire.

Un talk sur la transmission, et sur une tradition qui ne regarde pas en arrière : elle donne un futur au passé. Métallier-ferronnier d'art, Jim de Missolz s'est formé dix ans chez les Compagnons du Devoir, sur le Tour de France et ju
title: Reprendre le feu | Jim De Missolz | TEDxVersailles Grand Parc

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Il est né en Amérique du Sud il y a plus de 6 000 ans, et ses premiers passeurs furent des oiseaux. Puis Christophe Colomb l’a pris pour du poivre, les navigateurs portugais l’ont emporté jusqu’en Asie, et en moins d’un siècle le piment est devenu citoyen du monde.

Jean-Baptiste Martin raconte la trajectoire de cet « immigré exemplaire » et pourquoi on l’aime tant : il trompe notre cerveau en lui faisant croire à une brûlure, puis le récompense d’y avoir survécu. Il raconte aussi la sienne, de la cuisine d’un restaurant de San Francisco, où une cuillère de sauce pimentée lui a ouvert les portes de sa brigade mexicaine, à une pirogue en Amazonie équatorienne, chez les Siekopai, l’un des plus anciens peuples consommateurs de piment. Là-bas, personne n’enseignait : tout le monde apprenait.

Un talk sur la cuisine comme langage commun. Les frontières séparent parfois les hommes ; le piment, lui, les rassemble. Chef cuisinier, entrepreneur et explorateur du goût, Jean-Baptiste Martin est
title: Le piment, un passeport culturel | Jean-Baptiste Martin | TEDxVersailles Grand Parc

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Congressman Jake Auchincloss predicts that Big Tech will try to become Big Neuro by marketing brain-computer interfaces: electronic devices that directly translate brain activity into digital commands, or that induce brain activity by bypassing the usual sensory pathways. For example, imagine a microchip implant + injection that then allows you to use an app to put yourself to sleep, get into flow at work, or manage anxiety and depression. In this TEDx talk, Congressman Auchincloss raises three public policy questions that must be addressed to promote general welfare and prevent corporate exploitation if brain-computer interfaces scale to consumers. Congressman Jake Auchincloss is serving his third term representing the Massachusetts Fourth. In addition to his work on the House Committee on Energy & Commerce, his areas of focus include healthcare, clean energy, gun violence, and building a strong middle class.

title: Big Tech Wants to be Big Neuro. How Can Public Policy Respond? | Jake Auchincloss | TEDxBerkshires
